method.metric: Pearson lag-1 autocorrelation of each family’s target-level mean Top-5 hit share, computed within each chronological split.
method.selector_stability: Adjacent-target family selection agreement after the 100-target warm-up.
method.inferential_status: Descriptive only; no p-values or confirmatory claims; not included in the preregistered six-test family.

interpretation: Family target-level Top-5 outcomes show near-zero lag-1 persistence in Discovery and Validation, and negative mean lag-1 correlation in Blind OOS.
This is consistent with the rolling-100 selector failing to anticipate family usefulness; it is not proof of a causal mechanism.
The selector is relatively stable in its chosen family labels, but label stability does not translate into positive next-target family-performance lift.

Q90 equal-family mean Top-5 share is above the uniform 0.125 reference in Discovery (0.128466), below it in Validation (0.121131) and slightly below it in Blind OOS (0.124715). This pattern is consistent with Discovery feature-selection optimism, but does not isolate it from regime change or sampling variation.
limitations: Post-hoc descriptive analysis; no multiplicity-adjusted inferential test.
Only 700 deterministically sampled formulas from 330,429 Q90 formulas contribute to family outcomes.
Family outcomes are averages over sampled formulas and do not represent a deployable single formula.
next_action: Do not tune the rolling window from this diagnostic. Prioritize durable Q90 artifact import and typed AST reconciliation.
